channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Moraes mantém prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro e suspende visitas com finalidade 'político-eleitoral' até fim das Eleições 2026
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but suspended visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 Elections, also banning general visits for 30 days (except medical, physiotherapeutic, and legal). He further prohibited the dissemination of political-electoral manifestos by Bolsonaro or third parties, citing repeated violations of the precautionary measure, particularly through the 'Letter to Brazilians' involving his son Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Patrus Ananias conversa com Lula e deve ser anunciado ao governo de Minas na segunda
item.description: Federal deputy Patrus Ananias met with President Lula and is expected to be announced as the PT’s candidate for governor of Minas Gerais on Monday. His name emerged after refusals from Rodrigo Pacheco and Alexandre Kalil, aiming to secure a PT candidacy and a Lula-aligned platform in the state. PT Minas president Leninha said the meeting was positive and focused on education and state debt resolution.

item.title: PGR defende prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, mas pede regras mais rígidas
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) defended the maintenance of Jair Bolsonaro's humanitarian house arrest, but requested stricter rules for its enforcement. The manifestation was sent to Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF, after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro read and disclosed a letter written by the former president. The PGR argues that, despite the humanitarian concession, it is necessary to prevent abuses and ensure respect for judicial decisions.

item.title: PGR defende domiciliar a Bolsonaro, mas propõe veto a contatos que possam interferir nas eleições
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet advocated for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest, stating that the disclosure of a letter sent to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro does not override the humanitarian grounds for the measure. However, he proposed banning personal contacts that could interfere in the 2026 elections, calling the incident an opportunity to establish clear rules preventing the exploitation of Bolsonaro's actions to influence the vote. The final decision rests with Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: PGR defende manutenção da prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, mas vê violação em carta a Flávio
item.description: The PGR advocated for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but stated that the letter sent to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and disseminated on social media had a political-electoral purpose, violating STF-imposed restrictions. Despite the breach, the PGR deemed immediate return to closed custody disproportionate given Bolsonaro's health conditions, recommending clearer rules to prevent future misuse of personal contacts for electoral influence.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede autorização a Moraes para receber Milei
item.description: Lawyers for Jair Bolsonaro requested authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to allow a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei during Bolsonaro's house arrest, scheduled for July 25. The defense argues that the original visit restriction, based on Bolsonaro's fragile health, is no longer justified as the medical condition was transient. Milei is coming to Brazil to support Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign in 2026.

item.title: PGR defende manutenção de prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro apesar de carta
item.description: The PGR advocated for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest after his son, Flávio Bolsonaro, shared a video on social media reading a letter written by the former president. The PGR's statement came in response to the post, which may constitute a violation of the imposed precautionary measures.

item.title: Carta: Gonet diz que Bolsonaro violou cautelares, mas defende domiciliar
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet stated that Jair Bolsonaro violated precautionary measures by sending a letter to his son Flávio Bolsonaro, which was disseminated to influence the 2026 presidential race, yet argued against revoking house arrest, urging instead stricter rules to prevent further electoral interference.

item.title: PGR defende manutenção da prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro e que restrições sejam explicitadas
item.description: The PGR advocates for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest on humanitarian grounds, urging that communication restrictions be made explicit to prevent political misuse during the electoral period. This follows the dissemination of a letter by Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, on social media, deemed a violation of STF-imposed limits. The PGR argues the restrictions aim to block Bolsonaro's active political participation, given his penal conviction suspending his political rights.

item.title: PGR defende manutenção de prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, mas opina pela restrição de contatos do ex-presidente
item.description: The PGR advocated for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest, but acknowledged he violated STF restrictions by delivering a political letter to his son, Flávio Bolsonaro, intended to influence the electorate. Despite the violation, the PGR concluded the incident alone does not justify an immediate return to closed detention, as it would be disproportionate given the humanitarian circumstances. The office urged the STF to clarify house arrest conditions to prevent further electoral interference.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro pede autorização para visita de Milei ao ex-presidente
item.description: The defense of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro requested STF authorization for Argentine president Javier Milei to visit him under house arrest on July 25, 2026, during the PL party convention that will formalize Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential pre-candidacy. Milei had previously met with Flávio in June and stated he would travel to Brazil to support the Bolsonaro ticket, using the term 'blue tide' to describe the rise of right-wing politics in Latin America.

item.title: Moraes revoga uso de tornozeleira do youtuber Bismark Fugazza
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes revoked the electronic ankle monitor and nighttime/weekend house arrest for YouTuber Bismark Fugazza after over three years of full compliance with judicial measures without violations. Other restrictions, including a ban on social media use and contact with other January 8 investigators, remain in place. Fugazza welcomed the decision, emphasizing his adherence to the law and lack of conviction.

item.title: Bolsonaro pede autorização de Moraes para receber visita de Milei em prisão domiciliar
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro requested authorization from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to receive Argentine President Javier Milei at his residence, where he is serving house arrest, on April 25 at 4 p.m. The defense argues that the original medical restriction due to bronchopneumonia has lapsed and that the visit by a foreign head of state, previously announced and brief, should be approved under judicial oversight. Milei stated he would come to Brazil to support the presidential pre-candidacy of Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Com titulares, Flamengo está escalado para duelo contra o Olimpia
item.description: Flamengo is set to face Olimpia in a friendly match at Arena Mané Garrincha this Friday (July 17) at 8 PM, fielding its starting lineup as part of preparations for the resumption of the Brazilian and Paraguayan seasons. The club holds a strong record in the Federal District, with 42 wins in 76 matches, including a 5-1 victory over Olimpia in the 2021 Libertadores. Having recently won the Algarve Trophy in Portugal, Flamengo aims to conclude its preseason with another positive result.

item.title: Valdemar questiona possível vice de Flávio: “Ela não tem voto”
item.description: PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto stated that economist Daniella Marques lacks the electoral conditions to be vice president on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, saying 'she has no vote'. He indicated that the decision on the vice-presidential nominee could be postponed until after the party convention on July 25 in São Paulo.

item.title: Orientação de Lula após tarifaço é buscar novos mercados, diz Alckmin
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin stated that President Lula's orientation in response to the new U.S. tariff is to seek new international markets, emphasizing that negotiations are permanent and Brazil will defend its interests, jobs, and economy. He called the 25% tariff on Brazilian exports 'unjust and unfounded,' noting the U.S. maintains a trade surplus with Brazil. Alckmin cited Mercosul agreements with Singapore, EFTA, and the European Union, plus ongoing talks with Canada, Japan, Mexico, and the UAE as alternatives for trade diversion.

item.title: Ricardo Couto chora ao falar de Lula durante agenda do presidente no Rio
item.description: Acting Governor of Rio de Janeiro, Judge Ricardo Couto, became visibly emotional while praising President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's social sensitivity during a presidential agenda at the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation in Manguinhos. Couto thanked Lula for federal attention to Rio, citing initiatives like Propag and the Women's Health Caravan, and stated he lacks political 'clout' but possesses the sensitivity to govern with dignity. Lula embraced him and called Couto 'a chance God is giving this people,' saying no elected politician had ever generated such public expectation as he has.

item.title: PT anunciará na 2ª feira Patrus como candidato ao governo de MG
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) has designated Deputy Patrus Ananias as its pre-candidate for governor of Minas Gerais in the 2026 elections, with an official announcement scheduled for Monday, July 20. The decision followed consultations with national party leadership, including President Lula, after other potential candidates like Rodrigo Pacheco withdrew. Despite internal tensions over lack of consultation with the state directory, internal PT polls show Patrus at 15% voter intention, positioning him as a competitive option.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Daniella Marques 'não tem voto' para ser vice de Flávio e cogita arrastar definição para depois de convenção
item.description: PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto criticized economist Daniella Marques as a vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, stating she 'lacks votes' despite her competence and business elite prestige. He suggested the vice-presidential choice could be delayed until August 5, after the PL's July 25 convention, and named Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) as the ideal candidate due to her charisma and vote-pulling ability. However, Daniella's party (Republicanos) and the União Brasil-PP federation are expected to remain neutral in the presidential race.

item.title: Plataforma diz ser real tamanho de dedo de Sicário em foto com Flávio
item.description: The SignaIP platform concluded that the image of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário', was not AI-generated but authentic, based on pixel analysis, C2PA metadata, and a medical report confirming normal finger anatomy, attributing the elongated appearance to an optical illusion from finger overlap. ICL and InspireIP corroborated the findings, rejecting Bolsonaro's claim of AI manipulation. The case is tied to a PF investigation into an intimidation group linked to the founder of Banco Master.

item.title: O apelido de Flávio entre mulheres da direita após foto com Sicário
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro earned the nickname 'mitomaniac' among female right-wing leaders after claiming a photo with an individual known as 'Sicário' was AI-manipulated and denying he had seen a video released by Michelle Bolsonaro, despite its wide circulation among allies. The criticism emerged during a pre-campaign meeting, where his statements were viewed as dishonest and damaging to his credibility.

item.title: Lula diz que Ricardo Couto livrará Rio de Janeiro de milícias
item.description: Lula stated that Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Ricardo Couto, could rid the state of militias and criminal factions, praising his efforts to restore security for Fluminense workers. He highlighted Rio's political history and expressed hope that Couto would succeed where previous governors failed, following Cláudio Castro's resignation to run for the Senate in 2026.

item.title: Lula diz que usará “arma da palavra” contra Trump
item.description: President Lula stated he will use the 'weapon of words' to counter U.S. accusations over the tariff dispute, framing the response as a 'narrative war' rather than direct confrontation. He said he has already sent three messages to Trump, denying any desire for war and insisting on defending Brazil’s truth, while his administration calls U.S. claims false and politically motivated.

item.title: EUA tentaram limitar capital externo em minerais críticos do Brasil
item.description: The U.S. asked Brazil to limit foreign investment in critical minerals, particularly from non-market-oriented actors like China, during negotiations to avoid 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. The Lula government rejected the request, stating that critical minerals belong to the Brazilian people and that the demand overstepped trade boundaries, constituting an improper geopolitical restriction. The request was made only once in over 30 meetings during a year of negotiations.

item.title: Após operação da PF, governo de SP suspende contratação de consignados com banco Digimais
item.description: The São Paulo state government suspended new payroll-deductible loan contracts with bank Digimais following a Federal Police operation investigating the institution for alleged fraudulent management, false data insertion, and prohibited credit operations. The bank, linked to Bishop Edir Macedo, had 670 million reais frozen, with potential fraud costs reaching 12 billion reais for the Credit Guarantee Fund. The suspension, effective June 29, came two years after Governor Tarcísio de Freitas authorized military police to access Digimais payroll loans, despite a prior federal finance ministry rejection over regulatory non-compliance.

item.title: Lula: guerra que quero com Trump é a guerra da narrativa e da verdade
item.description: President Lula stated he does not seek armed conflict with Donald Trump, but rather a 'war of narrative and truth' regarding the 25% tariffs imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian exports. He emphasized that Brazil seeks peace but will defend its position with arguments and respect, awaiting a direct statement from Trump before issuing an official response.

item.title: 'Não saímos da mesa de negociação', diz Alckmin após Trump impor novo tarifaço a produtos brasileiros
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin stated that Brazil will not walk away from negotiations with the United States despite the new 25% tariff on Brazilian products, calling the measure unjust and unfounded. He emphasized that the Lula government supports free trade, is consulting affected sectors and seeking new markets, while President Lula said he will only comment on the issue after Donald Trump speaks publicly.

item.title: Lula diz querer fazer guerra da verdade com Trump sobre tarifaço
item.description: Lula said he wants to wage a 'truth war' with Trump over the U.S. tariff increase on Brazilian goods, emphasizing that Brazil seeks peace but will not avoid a narrative confrontation. He stated he will only respond when Trump speaks directly, criticizing that so far only U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has commented on the issue.

item.title: Adversários de Tarcísio exploram tarifaço enquanto governador evita o tema
item.description: Opponents of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) seized on Donald Trump’s tariff increases to criticize his administration in São Paulo, emphasizing the economic impacts on the state. Meanwhile, the governor avoided commenting on the issue, maintaining silence on the matter.

item.title: Rejeição ao bolsonarismo cresce e ao petismo cai, mostra pesquisa
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll showed that rejection of bolsonarism rose from 41% to 44% between June and July, reaching its highest level since February, while antipetism fell two points to 36%, continuing a downward trend since February when it was at 42%. The share of 'non-antibolsonarists' dropped from 56% to 51%, and 'non-antipetists' remained stable at 59%. The changes are within the poll's two-point margin of error.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Justiça Eleitoral vai aferir representação partidária para tempo de rádio e TV e debates
item.description: The Electoral Justice will verify on next Monday (20) the partisan representation in the Chamber of Deputies and the National Congress, based on the results of the 2022 General Elections. This verification will determine the free electoral airtime on radio and television, as well as party participation in electoral debates, as stipulated in the 2026 Electoral Calendar and regulated by the Elections Law and TSE Resolution No. 23.610/2019.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula fala em “guerra da palavra” com Trump
item.description: President Lula said he wants to engage in a 'war of words' with Donald Trump in response to the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian imports. He stated his goal is to prove to the world that Brazil is telling the truth in the trade dispute. Lula also criticized the press for finding it strange that he has not reacted more strongly to the tariff escalation.

item.title: Agenda Brasil Mais Saudável promove debate para jornalistas sobre políticas de saúde pública
item.description: ACT Health Promotion and Agência Bori are launching the second edition of the Brazil Healthier Agenda, an online event on July 29 from 10:00 to 11:30 for journalists. The discussion will focus on public policy proposals to prevent non-communicable chronic diseases and their inclusion in the 2026 election debate.

item.title: O Brasil interditado pelo governo
item.description: Brazil holds rare earth reserves equivalent to 186% of its GDP, yet remains unable to exploit them due to excessive bureaucracy, ideological environmentalism, legal insecurity, and lack of statesmanship. While neighboring countries like Guyana prosper through responsible natural resource exploitation, Brazil keeps strategic projects such as Ferrogrão and Margem Equatorial oil exploration stalled, turning potential wealth into poverty by political choice.

item.title: Nas redes, tarifaço deixa de ser pauta econômica para se tornar debate político, mostra estudo
item.description: The U.S. tariff hike has shifted from an economic issue to a political battle on social media, with the left defending national sovereignty and linking Flávio Bolsonaro to the policy, while the right accuses Lula of turning the crisis into an ideological clash with Washington. The media played a significant role, reflecting an unusual balance between political sides.

item.title: Dólar sobe 0,25% e Ibovespa cai 0,06% com tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The dollar rose 0.25% to close at R$ 5.111, while the Ibovespa fell 0.06% to 173,714 points, driven by investor reaction to the U.S. announcement of a 25% additional tariff on certain Brazilian imports, effective July 22. The Lula government is considering retaliatory measures, including the Economic Reciprocity Law, while pursuing diplomatic talks. The IBC-Br indicator showed 0.1% growth in May, signaling economic resilience.

item.title: Governo buscará exceções ao tarifaço, mas vê chance menor antes da eleição
item.description: The Brazilian government will continue diplomatic negotiations to secure exceptions to the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian products, but assesses that the likelihood of significant progress before the October presidential election is low.

item.title: Debate na TV é o fator que mais muda voto do eleitor, diz pesquisa
item.description: According to the Brazilian Electoral Panorama survey by Instituto Informa, 53.3% of Brazilian voters say live TV debates and interviews have the greatest potential to influence their vote choice, far surpassing social media (11.4%) and print/online news (22.3%). Conducted between May 21 and June 7, 2026 with 2,419 interviews, the study shows that while social media is the main entry point for political news, television retains higher credibility during electoral decision-making due to idea confrontation and spontaneity in debates.

item.title: Crusoé: Ricardo Couto pede reflexão antes do voto em evento com Lula
item.description: Interim Rio de Janeiro Governor Ricardo Couto urged voters in the state to reflect on their vote ahead of the October elections, speaking alongside President Lula. He emphasized the need to pay attention to the actions of candidates already known, suggesting caution based on political histories. The appeal was made during a joint event with Lula, highlighting the Presidency's support.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: O ‘Bolsa Telefone’ de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro introduced the 'Bolsa Telefone', promising free internet, cell phones, service apps, artificial intelligence, and daycare vouchers to attract female voters. The proposal was made during a live stream with Daniella Marques, economic advisor to his campaign, as part of a strategy to appeal to women.

item.title: Lula adia reação a novo tarifaço e avisa que EUA não ‘enganarão’ o Brasil
item.description: Lula avoided directly commenting on the new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, stating he will only respond after Donald Trump makes a public statement. He emphasized that Brazil will not be deceived and demanded reciprocity, asserting national sovereignty and resistance to unfair treatment. The 25% tariff could affect up to 36.5% of Brazil’s agribusiness exports to the U.S., according to the CNA.

item.title: Tarifaço: Lula diz que quer travar 'guerra da verdade' e que Trump vai ter que aprender a usar 'arma da palavra'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he wants to wage a 'narrative war, war of truth' with Donald Trump over the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, stating Brazil seeks peace but will defend truth and national respect. Lula emphasized that Trump must learn to fight with the 'weapon of words' and that Brazil will not allow its society to be deceived by the U.S. He affirmed Brazil’s sovereignty and the need to stand tall against international disrespect.

item.title: Sakamoto: Flávio dá vantagem a Lula ao se ligar cada vez mais ao tarifaço
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is giving an advantage to President Lula by increasingly aligning himself with the United States' tariff policy against Brazil, according to Leonardo Sakamoto's analysis on UOL News. This alignment with the US 'tariff war' is seen as a strategic mistake that strengthens Lula's position in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula diz que governador do Rio está 'fazendo um favor' ao estado no combate a milícias e facções
item.description: President Lula praised Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Claudio Coutinho, saying he is 'doing a favor' to the state in combating militias and factions during a visit to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics in downtown Rio. Lula noted that despite the governor's claim of not being a politician, he is acting responsibly ahead of the 2026 elections. The event also featured First Lady Janja, Mayor Eduardo Cavalieri, and Health Minister Alexandre Padilha, who emphasized federal support for security, health, and education in Rio.

item.title: Lula evita frenesi com pesquisas e pede ao time da campanha foco no trabalho e ‘pés no chão’
item.description: Lula urged allies and campaign staff to stay grounded despite his lead in polls over Flávio Bolsonaro, warning against complacency or a 'already won' mindset. He emphasized that with less than three months until the election, the focus must remain on hard work, campaign structuring, and showcasing his administration’s legacy and achievements. Lula noted that no opponent should be underestimated, as there is still time for shifts in voter sentiment.

item.title: Valdemar: ‘Paulo Figueiredo não sabe bulhufas e parece que trabalha para o PT’
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto criticized journalist Paulo Figueiredo for lacking political understanding, giving wrong opinions, and allegedly working for the PT, while also attacking women, particularly single women, claiming they 'vote badly'. He emphasized that Eduardo Bolsonaro remains a key electoral asset for the party, especially in São Paulo, and noted that Jair Bolsonaro’s rejection among women was decisive in his 2022 election loss.

item.title: A reação de Ciro Gomes à candidatura do irmão por uma chapa rival no Ceará
item.description: Ciro Gomes stated he always knew he and his brother Cid Gomes would end up facing each other electorally in 2026, as Cid seeks Senate re-election in a slate backed by Lula and Elmano, while Ciro runs for Ceará governor with a right-wing ticket. Cid justified his candidacy as a request from President Lula to strengthen the PT base, saying he is a 'soldier of the party'.

item.title: Terras raras: EUA pediu ao Brasil indiretamente para limitar investimentos da China
item.description: The U.S. government indirectly requested that Brazil limit Chinese investments in critical minerals and rare earths, framing the request as targeting 'extra-hemispheric' actors. Brazilian officials confirmed the request was made during high-level trade talks, with the U.S. citing agreements with the UK and Australia as precedents. Brazil rejected the demand, asserting sovereignty over its natural resources and stating that such decisions are not within U.S. jurisdiction, despite other American requests for market access and tariff reductions.

item.title: Brasil aceitou abrir mercado para tentar evitar tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government offered the U.S. tariff reductions on approximately 300 product lines — mainly industrial goods and technology — to avoid a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, while proposing ethanol market access contingent on U.S. tariff cuts on Brazilian sugar. It refused to negotiate on Pix, critical minerals, and China-related restrictions, deeming them non-negotiable. The proposal, submitted on July 2, aims to balance commercial concessions with protection of domestic industry.

item.title: Secretária dos EUA diz que Brasil fez comércio desleal e defende taxa
item.description: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins defended the 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, citing unfair trade practices and illegal deforestation. She criticized Brazil’s 18% tariff on U.S. ethanol, which cut American exports by over 87% since 2018. The tariff follows a Section 301 investigation by the USTR, which cites Pix and other sectors as creating unfair advantages for Brazil.
